title: Paired causal isolation of delta-bar-delta path memory on the real FGC44 carrier

technical_history.repair: Bind the fixed 12-call tail to the closed G21B result authority instead of a nonexistent G21B frozen_case.tail_calls member. No causal gate, solver configuration, response, threshold or production source changed.

bounded_conclusions: The closed G21B persistent prepared-solve path offset is reproduced exactly under the standard MODERATE delta-bar-delta configuration.
Disabling nonlinear under-relaxation from solver initialization changes NONMETH from 3 to 0 while preserving the frozen outer-2 response and accepted XOLD.

The intervention does not move the matched response roots at the strict G21 scale: the NOUR fresh outer-2 root error is zero and all three NOUR outer-1 history roots reproduce their frozen standard references exactly.
Under those matched conditions, the call-12 HISTORY-minus-FRESH offset collapses from 7.235112509107466e-11 m to -1.1102230246251565e-16 m, a 99.99984655068967% reduction in absolute offset.
This supports delta-bar-delta nonlinear under-relaxation history as a causal carrier of the strict prepared-solve path memory in this frozen real-FGC44 experiment.

The result does not imply that delta-bar-delta is physically or numerically wrong in MODFLOW, nor that production coupling should disable under-relaxation. It establishes a coupling-composition interaction when the externally assembled affine response is changed between solve calls.
G21 remains falsified as exact G17 trajectory equivalence under the standard configuration. G21D explains the dominant path-memory mechanism but does not retroactively change that verdict.
No production runtime, adapter, HCOF/RHS policy, E3/P4 rule or IMS configuration was changed.
